issues.description: Typo 'stlib' should be 'stdlib' in the deprecated directive.
issues.detail: The .. deprecated:: 4.3 block reads 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`'. This renders into published docs. Trivial fix in the same commit.

issues.description: Deprecation message should show the replacement for the both-streams case.
issues.detail: The warning and docstring name contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr but don't show how to compose them when a caller used redirected(stdout=a, stderr=b). One added clause pointing to nested with-statements or ExitStack would close the loop and also satisfy symmetry with the deprecated-since version.

issues.description: Test match pattern is loose and only covers the stdout path.
issues.detail: pytest.warns matches only the 'Please use...' suffix, so a reworded prefix passes silently; match on something stable like 'deprecated' or the function name. The test also exercises only stdout redirection — a symmetric stderr assertion would round out coverage while the function still ships.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this PR: a small, scoped deprecation of a bespoke redirected() wrapper in favor of stdlib contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr, with internal callers migrated, a news fragment added, and a warning test included. No correctness, performance, or architectural concerns were raised. The only consensus findings are minor polish items: a 'stlib' typo in the docstring, a deprecation message that should hand users the both-streams replacement, and a loose test match that only covers stdout. Fix the typo and ship.
